steps.title: Four sentences about the same day.
steps.sub: Two are arrangements with other people. Two are the speaker’s own intentions.

items.text: This morning I’m visiting a fashion show with colleagues.
I’m meeting a friend for lunch at one o’clock.
I’m going to look through some magazines this afternoon.
I’m going to change a few things.

steps.title: Look at the four sentences again.
steps.sub: I’m meeting a friend at one. · I’m going to look through some magazines.
steps.prompt: Which form does the speaker use for something already fixed with another person?
options: The Present Continuous: I’m meeting a friend at one.
going to: I’m going to meet a friend some time.
Both forms mean exactly the same thing here.
steps.answer: The Present Continuous: I’m meeting a friend at one.
steps.why: The Present Continuous is for arrangements — a time, a place, another person. Going to is for an intention or a prediction.

steps.title: Two ways of talking about the future
steps.html:
going to — intention or planPresent Continuous — arrangement
I’m going to spend 24 hours offline.I’m meeting a friend at one o’clock.
I’m going to walk 10,000 steps a day.I’m visiting a fashion show this morning.
We aren’t going to eat meat for 30 days.My parents are coming for lunch on Sunday.
What are you going to do first?Are you doing anything on Friday night?
It’s not going to be easy.A few of us are meeting next Saturday.

going to = am / is / are + going to + base verb. Use it for what you have decided to do, and for what you can see is going to happen.

Present Continuous = am / is / are + -ing. Use it for an arrangement: a time and usually another person are already fixed.

Both need a future time word when the meaning could be “now”: this afternoon, tomorrow, on Sunday, next week.

In speech going to often sounds like gonna. Write going to.

will and might for predictions come in Unit 7, Lesson 19.

steps.prompt: You have a ticket and a seat number for tomorrow’s train. Which is better?
options: I’m travelling to Astana tomorrow.

steps.answer: I’m travelling to Astana tomorrow.
steps.why: It is arranged, with a time → Present Continuous.
